views.name: section_with_course_instructor_room_time
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id AS course_id,
  s.sec_id AS sec_id,
  s.semester AS semester,
  s.year AS year,
  s.building AS building,
  s.room_number AS room_number,
  s.time_slot_id AS time_slot_id,
  c.title AS title,
  c.dept_name AS dept_name,
  c.credits AS credits,
  t.ID AS ID,
  i.name AS name,
  i.dept_name AS instructor_dept_name,
  cl.capacity AS capacity,
  ts.day AS day,
  ts.start_hr AS start_hr,
  ts.start_min AS start_min,
  ts.end_hr AS end_hr,
  ts.end_min AS end_min
FROM section s
LEFT JOIN course c
  ON s.course_id = c.course_id
LEFT JOIN teaches t
  ON s.course_id = t.course_id
  AND s.sec_id = t.sec_id
  AND s.semester = t.semester
  AND s.year = t.year
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON t.ID = i.ID
LEFT JOIN classroom cl
  ON s.building = cl.building
  AND s.room_number = cl.room_number
LEFT JOIN time_slot ts
  ON s.time_slot_id = ts.time_slot_id

params.description: Provides one row per course section offering with its course info, assigned instructor (if any), classroom, and time slot details.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve detailed schedule and staffing info for a specific course section (by course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | List all sections with room, time, and instructor attributes for timetabling or display. | Compose counts or aggregations by joining this view with enrollment/attendance or other many-side facts (with care). | Filter sections by instructor, building, time slot attributes, or course attributes and then aggregate.
params.output_schema: course_id: course identifier — derived from section.course_id (s.course_id) | sec_id: section identifier within the course offering — derived from section.sec_id (s.sec_id) | semester: academic term label for the section — derived from section.semester (s.semester) | year: calendar/academic year for the section — derived from section.year (s.year) | building: building code/name where the section meets — derived from section.building (s.building) | room_number: room identifier within the building — derived from section.room_number (s.room_number) | time_slot_id: foreign key to time_slot identifying the meeting time — derived from section.time_slot_id (s.time_slot_id) | title: course title — derived from course.title (c.title) via LEFT JOIN on course.course_id = section.course_id | dept_name: course's department name — derived from course.dept_name (c.dept_name) | credits: course credit value — derived from course.credits (c.credits) | ID: instructor ID assigned to teach this section (may be NULL if no teaches row) — derived from teaches.ID (t.ID) | name: instructor name — derived from instructor.name (i.name) via LEFT JOIN on instructor.ID = teaches.ID | instructor_dept_name: instructor's department name — derived from instructor.dept_name (i.dept_name) | capacity: classroom capacity for the assigned room (may be NULL if no matching classroom) — derived from classroom.capacity (cl.capacity) | day: day code for the time slot (may be NULL if no matching time_slot) — derived from time_slot.day (ts.day) | start_hr: start hour of the time slot — derived from time_slot.start_hr (ts.start_hr) | start_min: start minute of the time slot — derived from time_slot.start_min (ts.start_min) | end_hr: end hour of the time slot — derived from time_slot.end_hr (ts.end_hr) | end_min: end minute of the time slot — derived from time_slot.end_min (ts.end_min)
params.grounded_columns: section.course_id | section.sec_id | section.semester | section.year | section.building | section.room_number | section.time_slot_id | course.course_id | course.title | course.dept_name | course.credits | teaches.course_id | teaches.sec_id | teaches.semester | teaches.year | teaches.ID | instructor.ID | instructor.name | instructor.dept_name | classroom.building | classroom.room_number | classroom.capacity | time_slot.time_slot_id | time_slot.day | time_slot.start_hr | time_slot.start_min | time_slot.end_hr | time_slot.end_min
params.metric: This view is at a strict section-grain: no aggregated metrics are defined here. All columns are direct projections (no SUM/COUNT/AVG). If you need counts (e.g., enrolled students), compute them by aggregating a many-side table (student_enrollment_counts or takes_with_student_course_section) after joining — do not assume any pre-aggregation in this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course on course_id — safe because this view contains at most one course row per section (course is a 1:1 or many:1 reference from section to course), so joining course would not duplicate rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to time_slot on time_slot_id — safe because section.time_slot_id is a single FK; joining time_slot returns at most one matching row per section and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom is referenced by section's building+room; this is at most one matching classroom per section and will not duplicate rows. | cardinality-CAUTION: joining to teaches as present in this view is LEFT JOINed and may already produce duplicate instructor rows if the teaches table can have multiple rows per section (e.g., multiple instructor assignments). The view as defined joins teaches without deduplication, so the view's grain is the combination [course_id, sec_id, semester, year, ID] — caution callers: if teaches contains multiple rows per section (different IDs), this view will contain multiple rows per section (one per teaches row). The declared grain reflects ID as part of the view key to capture that possibility. | cardinality-CAUTION: do NOT join this view to another one-to-many table (for example, a table of enrolled students or meeting exceptions) without first aggregating the many-side to the same grain. Joining a many-side (student enrollments, multiple instructors, multiple meeting times) directly will multiply the view's rows and any downstream aggregates. Instead, aggregate the many-side to counts or other metrics grouped by (course_id, sec_id, semester, year, ID) or by the section key (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) depending on whether you intend to preserve instructor-level uniqueness. | safe composition examples: | - To get enrollment counts per section: LEFT JOIN an aggregated enrollment table grouped by (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) (e.g., student_enrollment_counts aggregated to that key). This is safe because the enrollment side was reduced to one row per section before joining. | - To compute capacity utilization per section: join classroom (safe) and then join aggregated enrollment counts by section (safe if aggregated first). | unsafe composition examples: | - Do NOT directly join the raw student enrollment table (many students per section) to this view and then SUM without re-aggregating, because each student row will duplicate section-level attributes and overcount. | - Do NOT join a raw teaches table to this view unless you intend to expand by instructor (this view already includes teaches — joining another raw teaches table risks duplication). | keys to use when joining: | - Section-level joins: use (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — this is the natural section key when you want one-row-per-section. If you need instructor-level rows, include ID in the join key as this view exposes ID in its grain. | - Course-level joins: use course_id only (safe, 1:1 from course to view per section).

views.description: One row per section offering enriched with course title/credits, instructor(s) assigned, classroom info and time slot details. Useful when answering questions about offerings, who teaches them, where/when they meet, or joining to enrollments or grades. | Use for: List sections with instructor and room/time details; Which instructor teaches a given section or course offering; Where and when is a section held and what is the classroom capacity; Join sections to enrollments or grades

views.name: takes_with_student_course_section
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tk.ID AS ID,
  s.name AS name,
  s.dept_name AS dept_name,
  s.tot_cred AS tot_cred,
  tk.course_id AS course_id,
  tk.sec_id AS sec_id,
  tk.semester AS semester,
  tk.year AS year,
  tk.grade AS grade,
  c.title AS title,
  c.credits AS credits,
  t.ID AS instructor_ID,
  i.name AS instructor_name
FROM takes tk
LEFT JOIN student s
  ON tk.ID = s.ID
LEFT JOIN course c
  ON tk.course_id = c.course_id
LEFT JOIN teaches t
  ON tk.course_id = t.course_id
  AND tk.sec_id = t.sec_id
  AND tk.semester = t.semester
  AND tk.year = t.year
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON t.ID = i.ID

params.description: Provides one row per student-course-section enrollment (a student's taking of a specific course section in a term), with student, course, and instructor attributes.
params.when_to_use: List or filter enrollments (who took which course section in which term) and show student, course, and instructor attributes in the same row. | Compose additional aggregations about enrollments (counts, grade distributions) by grouping this view by its grain (ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | Join with other dimension-like views (e.g., time_slot_readable, section_with_course_instructor_room_time) to enrich section metadata while preserving enrollment-level semantics. | Filter enrollments by student attributes (dept_name, tot_cred), course attributes (title, credits), instructor attributes (instructor_name) before further aggregation.
params.output_schema: ID: student identifier — from takes.ID (tk.ID) | name: student name — from student.name (s.name) via LEFT JOIN on tk.ID = s.ID | dept_name: student's department name — from student.dept_name (s.dept_name) | tot_cred: student's total credits — from student.tot_cred (s.tot_cred) | course_id: course identifier for the section — from takes.course_id (tk.course_id) | sec_id: section identifier within the course offering — from takes.sec_id (tk.sec_id) | semester: term semester token (e.g., Fall) — from takes.semester (tk.semester) | year: term year — from takes.year (tk.year) | grade: grade earned by the student in that section — from takes.grade (tk.grade) | title: course title — from course.title (c.title) via LEFT JOIN on tk.course_id = c.course_id | credits: course credits — from course.credits (c.credits) | instructor_ID: instructor identifier for the section — from teaches.ID (t.ID) via LEFT JOIN matching course_id, sec_id, semester, year | instructor_name: instructor name — from instructor.name (i.name) via LEFT JOIN on t.ID = i.ID
params.grounded_columns: takes.ID | takes.course_id | takes.sec_id | takes.semester | takes.year | takes.grade | student.ID | student.name | student.dept_name | student.tot_cred | course.course_id | course.title | course.credits | teaches.ID | teaches.course_id | teaches.sec_id | teaches.semester | teaches.year | instructor.ID | instructor.name
params.metric: This view is at the raw enrollment grain; it does not define aggregated metrics itself. Use GROUP BY on the view's grain or subsets to derive metrics. Example derived metrics you can compute safely from this view: | enrollment_count = COUNT(*) grouped by (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) -> counts takes rows (one row per enrollment). | avg_grade = AVG(grade) grouped by (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) -> average of takes.grade for the section (note: grade must be numeric/mapped prior to AVG). | distinct_student_count = COUNT(DISTINCT ID) when aggregating across grouping keys that could span student duplicates.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: | Join to student (or a student dimension view) on takes_with_student_course_section.ID = student.ID — safe because this view already left-joined student at 1:1 on student.ID; joining to a properly key'd student dimension (one row per student.ID) will not duplicate measures. | Join to course (or a course dimension view) on course_id = course.course_id — safe if the target is one row per course_id (course dimension). The view already joins course by course_id; joining to a course dimension keyed by course_id will not multiply rows. | Join to instructor (or an instructor dimension view) on instructor_ID = instructor.ID — safe if the target is one row per instructor.ID. The view exposes at most one instructor_ID per enrollment row (from teaches), so joining to a 1:1 instructor dimension does not duplicate. | Join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — safe if that view is one row per section (course_id, sec_id, semester, year). Because this view's grain is enrollment (one or more enrollments per section), joining to one-row-per-section enriches each enrollment without duplicating enrollment measures. |  | do NOT join without care (these joins will multiply rows/measures unless you re-aggregate): | Do NOT join to teaches (or any view/table that is one-to-many from section to rows) on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) if that target can contain multiple rows per section (e.g., multiple teach records per section) — that would duplicate enrollment rows and any derived counts/aggregates unless you first aggregate the teaches side to one row per section or re-aggregate after the join. | Do NOT join to course_prereq_edges (an edge/one-to-many per course) directly when computing section- or enrollment-level aggregates without re-aggregation on the prerequisite side; prereq edges are many-per-course and would multiply rows per enrollment for the same course_id. | Do NOT join to any aggregation view that is at a finer grain (e.g., instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester that lists multiple ranked rows per instructor-section combination) unless you aggregate that view to one row per join key first. |  | Practical composition rules for planners: | - If you need to enrich enrollment rows with data that is one-to-many from the join key, either (a) aggregate that many-side to one row per join key before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate the final result grouping by the enrollment grain (ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year) so measures like enrollment_count are recomputed correctly. | - This view's measures and implicit unit of analysis are per takes row (enrollment). Treat it as one-row-per-enrollment when composing; do not assume it is pre-aggregated to section level.

views.description: One row per student enrollment (takes) with student demographic info and course/section metadata (title, credits, semester/year, instructor if any). Use for grade reports, per-student transcripts, or course-level enrollment analyses. | Use for: Student transcript / grades per term; Which students took a given course offering; Combine enrollment with instructor to see which instructor taught which students

views.name: course_prereq_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.course_id AS course_id,
  p.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq p

params.description: Lists direct prerequisite edges between courses (one row per course -> prerequisite pair).
params.when_to_use: Find all direct prerequisites for a given course_id or set of course_ids | Build prerequisite graphs, transitive-closure or path-finding queries when combined with self-joins or graph algorithms | Filter or join course-level datasets to restrict/annotate by whether a course has a particular prerequisite | Compose into aggregates like count of prerequisites per course (must re-aggregate after joins that can multiply rows)
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course that has a prerequisite — derived from base column prereq.course_id | prereq_id: identifier of the course that is required as a prerequisite — derived from base column prereq.prereq_id
params.metric: no derived measures in this view; all outputs are base keys (course_id and prereq_id) directly projected from prereq table
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course dimension or course metadata tables/views on course_id (e.g., join course_prereq_edges.course_id = course.course_id) — safe because this view is one-row-per (course_id, prereq_id) and joining to a one-row-per-course dimension will not duplicate edges beyond the natural 1-to-1/1-to-0 relationship | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course dimension or course metadata on prereq_id = course.course_id to bring metadata for the prerequisite course — safe for the same reason (one-row-per-course dimension) | do NOT directly join to one-to-many fact or detail views (for example, section_with_course_instructor_room_time, takes_with_student_course_section, instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester, or any enrollment/section-level views) without re-aggregating, because those joins can multiply rows per (course_id, prereq_id) and thus would multiply any counts derived from this view | if you need aggregates that combine prerequisite edges with section- or student-level data (e.g., number of students affected by a prerequisite), first aggregate the one-to-many side to a single row per course_id (or per course_id+term as appropriate), then join to course_prereq_edges on course_id to avoid duplication | self-joins of this view (e.g., to compute two-step prerequisites) are safe in the sense they correctly expand the edge-set—these will increase row counts because they produce composed paths; treat resulting rows as edges/paths and re-aggregate if you need per-course summaries | example safe composition: to get count of direct prerequisites per course, perform SELECT course_id, COUNT(*) FROM course_prereq_edges GROUP BY course_id — do not join other one-to-many tables before counting unless you intend to count multiplied combinations

views.description: One row per direct prerequisite edge (course -> prereq). Use as the base edge set for recursive traversal to find full prerequisite chains or to detect cycles. | Use for: Compute full prerequisite chains via recursive traversal; Detect cycles in course prerequisites; Find all immediate prerequisites for a course

views.name: instructor_salary_by_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(ID) AS instructor_count,
  AVG(salary) AS avg_salary,
  MIN(salary) AS min_salary,
  MAX(salary) AS max_salary,
  SUM(salary) AS total_salary
FROM instructor
GROUP BY dept_name

params.description: Aggregated instructor salary statistics per department (counts and summary salary metrics).
params.when_to_use: Report total and summary salary statistics for each department (count of instructors, avg/min/max/sum of salary). | Compare departments by average or total instructor salary. | As a base aggregate when composing higher-level metrics by department (e.g., salary per student when joined safely to department-level student counts). | Filterable departmental salary summaries (e.g., show departments with avg_salary > X).
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (sourced from instructor.dept_name) | instructor_count: number of instructors in the department (COUNT(instructor.ID)) | avg_salary: average instructor salary for the department (AVG(instructor.salary)) | min_salary: minimum instructor salary in the department (MIN(instructor.salary)) | max_salary: maximum instructor salary in the department (MAX(instructor.salary)) | total_salary: sum of instructor salaries in the department (SUM(instructor.salary))
params.metric: instructor_count = COUNT(instructor.ID) -- cardinality of instructors grouped by instructor.dept_name | avg_salary = AVG(instructor.salary) -- mean salary among instructors in each dept_name | min_salary = MIN(instructor.salary) -- minimum salary among instructors in each dept_name | max_salary = MAX(instructor.salary) -- maximum salary among instructors in each dept_name | total_salary = SUM(instructor.salary) -- sum of salaries among instructors in each dept_name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or view that is one-row-per-department (e.g., a canonical department dimension view keyed by dept_name) on dept_name — safe because instructor_salary_by_department is one-row-per-dept_name and its aggregated measures will not be duplicated. | You may safely join to course_offering_counts_by_term or course_popularity_by_enrollment only if those views are pre-aggregated to one-row-per-dept_name (they are not declared as such here). If you need department-level course metrics, first aggregate those views to dept_name before joining, or perform a SQL join followed by re-aggregation on dept_name to avoid duplication. | Do NOT directly join instructor_salary_by_department to one-to-many tables/views keyed to department (for example: section_with_course_instructor_room_time, takes_with_student_course_section, student_enrollment_counts if it is one-row-per-student) without re-aggregating the one-to-many side to dept_name first — such joins will duplicate instructor_count and total_salary because instructor_salary_by_department already holds aggregated sums/counts per dept_name. | If you need per-department ratios (e.g., salary per enrolled student), obtain the other measure at dept_name granularity (for example, aggregate student_enrollment_counts to dept_name or join student_latest_advisor -> student -> department and aggregate) and then join one-row-per-dept_name to this view so that measures align and are not multiplied. | If composing with ranked or recursive views (e.g., instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester or course_prereq_edges), ensure those are reduced to dept_name-level aggregates or filtered to one-row-per-dept_name before joining to preserve measure correctness. | General rule: treat this view as authoritative one-row-per(dept_name) metrics. Only join other datasets that are also one-row-per(dept_name) or perform aggregation after any join to restore dept_name granularity.

views.description: Department-level aggregates of instructor counts and salary measures (count, avg_salary, min_salary, max_salary, total_salary). Useful for budgeting, staffing and pay-distribution questions. | Use for: Compare departments by instructor headcount or total/avg salary; Detect departments with unusually high/low average pay; Budget planning based on instructor salaries

views.name: course_offering_counts_by_term
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course_id AS course_id,
  semester AS semester,
  year AS year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sec_id) AS sections_offered
FROM section
GROUP BY course_id, semester, year

params.description: Counts of distinct sections offered for each course in each semester and year.
params.when_to_use: How many sections were offered for a given course in a specific semester and year? | Comparing section supply across courses, semesters, or years (e.g., trend analysis of sections offered). | As a building block when computing course-level supply metrics (e.g., sections per course per term) or joining to enrollment/room/instructor data after ensuring cardinality safety.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course — derived from section.course_id | semester: academic term label (e.g., 'Fall', 'Spring') — derived from section.semester | year: calendar/academic year of the offering — derived from section.year | sections_offered: the number of distinct section instances (sec_id) offered for that course in that semester and year — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT section.sec_id)
params.metric: sections_offered = COUNT(DISTINCT section.sec_id)  -- distinct count of sec_id per (course_id, semester, year)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like or one-row-per-course/per-term views on (course_id, semester, year) — safe because course_offering_counts_by_term has one row per (course_id, semester, year) and its sections_offered measure will not be duplicated. Example: join to course_popularity_by_enrollment on (course_id, semester, year) if that view is also one-row-per-(course_id,semester,year). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., section, takes_with_student_course_section, section_with_course_instructor_room_time) on course_id without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply rows and thus inflate sections_offered. If you need details from section (or other one-to-many children), either: 1) join this view to a pre-aggregated child keyed at (course_id, semester, year), or 2) join at finer grain and recompute/aggregate sections (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT sec_id) in the composed query) so the measure is correct. | Safe composition examples: | - Join to instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester only if that view returns one row per (course_id, semester, year) or you first reduce it to one row per (course_id, semester, year). | - Join to student_enrollment_counts aggregated to (course_id, semester, year) to compute sections_offered per enrolled student. | Unsafe composition examples: | - Joining to section (raw) on course_id + term will duplicate sections_offered because section contains multiple sec_id rows for the same (course_id, semester, year). | - Joining to takes_with_student_course_section (student-level enrollment rows) on course_id + term will multiply sections_offered by student count; re-aggregate after join or pre-aggregate student rows first. | General rule: treat sections_offered as a term-level aggregate; only join to other datasets that are at the same (course_id, semester, year) grain or have been reduced/aggregated to that grain before combining, otherwise recompute the distinct-section count at the desired final grain.

views.description: Counts of distinct section offerings per course per semester/year. Use to find how often a course is offered, trending offer frequency, or to join with enrollment counts. | Use for: How many sections of a course were offered in a term; Identify courses with growing/shrinking offering counts; Prepare denominator for enrollment per-section metrics

views.name: student_enrollment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tk.ID AS ID,
  COUNT(*) AS enrollments_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tk.course_id) AS distinct_courses_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tk.semester || '_' || tk.year) AS distinct_terms_count
FROM takes tk
GROUP BY tk.ID

params.description: Per-student (ID) aggregate counts of enrollments, distinct courses taken, and distinct term occurrences, answering how many times and in how many unique courses/terms each student has enrolled.
params.when_to_use: Get totals per student: total enrollments, how many distinct courses a student has taken, and how many distinct terms the student has been enrolled in. | Filter or rank students by activity (most enrolled courses, most terms attended) when building reports or dashboards. | Compose with student demographic or advisor data (one-to-one) to show these counts alongside student attributes. | As a pre-aggregated building block for further aggregation (e.g., department-level or advisor-level summaries) by re-aggregating these per-student measures.
params.output_schema: ID: student identifier — sourced from takes.ID (GROUP BY tk.ID). This is the grain of the view (one row per student ID). | enrollments_count: number of enrollment records for the student = COUNT(*) from takes (counts rows in takes for that ID). | distinct_courses_count: number of distinct courses the student has taken = COUNT(DISTINCT tk.course_id) from takes. | distinct_terms_count: number of distinct terms the student has been enrolled in = COUNT(DISTINCT tk.semester || '_' || tk.year) computed from takes.semester and takes.year concatenation.
params.metric: enrollments_count = COUNT(*) over rows of takes grouped by takes.ID | distinct_courses_count = COUNT(DISTINCT takes.course_id) grouped by takes.ID | distinct_terms_count = COUNT(DISTINCT (takes.semester || '_' || takes.year)) grouped by takes.ID
params.composition: Join to student_dimension (or any one-row-per-student view/table) on ID — safe because student_enrollment_counts is one-row-per-ID; joining retains 1:1 cardinality so the aggregated measures are not duplicated. | Join to student_latest_advisor on ID — safe (one-row-per-student) for showing advisor with these counts without re-aggregation. | Do NOT directly join to takes (or any other one-to-many child of student) on ID without re-aggregating afterwards — unsafe because takes is many-per-student and would multiply enrollments_count and distinct_* measures. | Do NOT join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time or instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester without ensuring those joins are reduced to one row per student (e.g., pre-aggregate or join on a single chosen key) — those views are many-to-many relative to students and would duplicate this view's measures if joined directly. | To roll up to advisor- or department-level aggregates: first join this view to a one-row-per-student dimension that carries advisor/department, then SUM(enrollments_count), SUM(distinct_courses_count) requires careful semantics (distinct_counts cannot be summed across students to get distinct students-level distinct values). For distinct counts at higher grain, re-compute from base takes or use distinct-aware techniques (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT course_id) over appropriate grouping on takes) rather than summing distinct_courses_count. | When composing with other AGG sibling views (e.g., course_offering_counts_by_term or course_popularity_by_enrollment), prefer joining on keys where one side is one-row-per-key; if both sides are aggregated at different grains, align grains or re-aggregate to avoid duplication.

views.description: Per-student counts of enrollments and distinct courses taken, plus number of distinct semesters attended. Useful for student activity summaries, retention metrics, or filtering active students. | Use for: How many courses a student has taken; Identify inactive students by term counts; Prepare per-student cohorts for advising

views.name: instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ID AS ID,
  t.course_id AS course_id,
  t.sec_id AS sec_id,
  t.semester AS semester,
  t.year AS year,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.ID ORDER BY t.year DESC, t.semester DESC) AS teaching_rank
FROM teaches t

params.description: Ranks each instructor's teaching assignments (teaches rows) by year and semester, newest first.
params.when_to_use: Find the most recent (or nth most recent) section an instructor taught. | Filter or order an instructor's teaches records by recency within that instructor. | Compose queries that need a teaching-rank per teaches row (e.g., join to only each instructor's latest teaching assignment). | Build time-aware metrics per instructor by selecting top-N ranked teaching assignments before aggregating.
params.output_schema: ID: instructor identifier from teaches.ID (base column teaches.ID). | course_id: course identifier for the teaching assignment from teaches.course_id (base column teaches.course_id). | sec_id: section identifier for the teaching assignment from teaches.sec_id (base column teaches.sec_id). | semester: semester label for the teaching assignment from teaches.semester (base column teaches.semester). | year: year for the teaching assignment from teaches.year (base column teaches.year). | teaching_rank: integer rank of this teaches row within the same instructor (teaches.ID), ordered by year DESC, semester DESC; implemented as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY teaches.ID ORDER BY teaches.year DESC, teaches.semester DESC).
params.metric: teaching_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY teaches.ID ORDER BY teaches.year DESC, teaches.semester DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor dimension tables or views keyed by ID (e.g., join to a table/view that has one row per instructor on ID) — safe because instructor_sections_ranked_by_year_semester is one (or more) row(s) per teaches assignment and joining a one-row-per-instructor dimension will not duplicate its rows. | Join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time on (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) — safe when that view is one-row-per-section offering (i.e., it does not replicate sections). If section_with_course_instructor_room_time is one-row-per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year), measures (teaching_rank) are not duplicated. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as takes_with_student_course_section, student_enrollment_counts (per student), or course_prereq_edges without careful aggregation/filters first — these are one-to-many relative to a teaches row and would multiply teaching_rank-bearing rows and thus duplicate counts/measures. | If you need to combine with enrollment or student-level details, either: a) aggregate the many-side to one row per (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) before joining (e.g., enrollment count per section), or b) join and then re-aggregate with GROUP BY on the view's grain (ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year) to avoid double-counting. | When selecting only the latest teaching assignment per instructor, filter where teaching_rank = 1; that returns at most one row per instructor (ID). Such a result can safely be joined to instructor-level tables on ID without creating duplicates. | If you need stable tie-breaking beyond semester and year, be aware RANK() can produce ties; joining logic that expects unique latest row per instructor should handle possible multiple rank=1 rows (e.g., by adding additional deterministic ordering or using ROW_NUMBER() in a derived query). | Do NOT assume teaching_rank is an aggregate metric across joins — it is a windowed rank per teaches row. When composing metrics that sum or average across instructors, ensure you aggregate after any joins at the intended grain (typically per ID or per section) to avoid miscounting.

views.description: Per-instructor chronological ranking of the sections they taught, ordered by year then semester. Exposes a rank so callers can select the most recent or top-N taught sections per instructor. | Use for: Find most recent sections taught by an instructor (WHERE teaching_rank = 1); Top-N recent courses per instructor; Temporal analysis of instructor workload

views.name: student_latest_advisor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.s_ID AS s_ID,
  a.i_ID AS i_ID,
  i.name AS name
FROM advisor a
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON a.i_ID = i.ID

params.description: For each student (s_ID), returns that student's latest recorded advisor instructor id and that instructor's name as available via the advisor -> instructor left join.
params.when_to_use: Find the advisor (instructor id and name) associated with a particular student id. | Enrich student-level records with their advisor's instructor id or name when each student has at most one advisor row in the advisor table (the view is one-row-per s_ID). | Compose student-level reporting or joins where advisor attributes are needed (e.g., list students with their advisor names). | Filter or group students by advisor instructor id or advisor instructor name.
params.output_schema: s_ID: student identifier — derived from advisor.s_ID (a.s_ID AS s_ID). Grain: one row per advisor.s_ID as produced by the advisor table. | i_ID: advisor instructor identifier — derived from advisor.i_ID (a.i_ID AS i_ID). Null if advisor.i_ID is NULL. | name: instructor name — derived from instructor.name (i.name AS name) via LEFT JOIN from advisor.i_ID to instructor.ID. Null if no matching instructor.
params.metric: No aggregates in this view. All outputs are direct column projections / lookups. | s_ID = advisor.s_ID (identity projection) | i_ID = advisor.i_ID (identity projection) | name = instructor.name (lookup via join)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to student-level or one-row-per-student dimensions on s_ID — e.g., join to a students table or a student profile view on student.ID = student_latest_advisor.s_ID is safe because student_latest_advisor is one-row-per s_ID, so it will not duplicate advisor attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructor-level dimensions on i_ID — e.g., join to instructor details on instructor.ID = student_latest_advisor.i_ID is safe because instructor is keyed by ID (one row per instructor). This will not duplicate advisor measures. | DO NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many child table keyed by s_ID (for example a takes, section, or enrollment table) without re-aggregation or shifting the join direction, because those tables can have multiple rows per s_ID and would multiply the student_latest_advisor rows. If you need to combine with a many-rows-per-student relation, either: | - aggregate the child relation up to s_ID first (e.g., count courses per s_ID) and then join to student_latest_advisor on s_ID, or | - join student_latest_advisor onto the many-side (i.e., start from the many-side table and LEFT JOIN student_latest_advisor) so advisor attributes are repeated per many-side row intentionally. | Specific examples of unsafe joins without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to takes_with_student_course_section (which is many rows per student), student_enrollment_counts (if that view is aggregated to student it's okay — verify grain), or section_with_course_instructor_room_time if it contains multiple sections per student, unless you aggregate first by s_ID. | Safe composition with sibling views depends on their grain: | - Safe: join to views with grain = student (one row per s_ID) or instructor (one row per instructor.ID) on matching keys — these joins will not duplicate rows. | - Caution: do NOT join to sibling JOIN/REC/AGG/RANK views that are many-to-one or one-to-many on s_ID without handling multiplicity. For example, joining to takes_with_student_course_section (likely many per student) will multiply rows; instead aggregate takes to one row per s_ID (e.g., course_count) before joining. | Rationale: this view's measures are not aggregated — they are direct attributes at the s_ID grain. Any join to a table with multiple rows per s_ID will multiply these attribute rows unless the downstream query re-aggregates or the join direction ensures repetition is expected.

views.description: One row per student with their advisor ID and advisor name. Useful for routing advising communications or joining advisor attributes to student cohorts. | Use for: Lookup advisor for a given student; List advisors and their advisees; Join advisor info into student-level reports

views.name: time_slot_readable
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  time_slot_id AS time_slot_id,
  day AS day,
  start_hr AS start_hr,
  start_min AS start_min,
  end_hr AS end_hr,
  end_min AS end_min,
  printf('%02d:%02d', start_hr, start_min) AS start_time_text,
  printf('%02d:%02d', end_hr, end_min) AS end_time_text
FROM time_slot

params.description: Provides a human-readable representation of time slots (start/end hours and minutes and formatted HH:MM text) for each time_slot_id and day.
params.when_to_use: Display or report time slot labels (e.g., show '09:30' - '10:45') for a given time_slot_id or day. | Join time slot textual labels into schedules, sections, or room assignments to render readable start/end times. | Filter or group by start/end hour or minute components when composing higher-level queries (e.g., find all slots starting at a given hour).
params.output_schema: time_slot_id: unique identifier of the time slot (derived from time_slot.time_slot_id) | day: day indicator for the time slot (derived from time_slot.day) | start_hr: integer hour when the slot starts (derived from time_slot.start_hr) | start_min: integer minute when the slot starts (derived from time_slot.start_min) | end_hr: integer hour when the slot ends (derived from time_slot.end_hr) | end_min: integer minute when the slot ends (derived from time_slot.end_min) | start_time_text: formatted start time as zero-padded 'HH:MM' (expression: printf('%02d:%02d', start_hr, start_min) using time_slot.start_hr and time_slot.start_min) | end_time_text: formatted end time as zero-padded 'HH:MM' (expression: printf('%02d:%02d', end_hr, end_min) using time_slot.end_hr and time_slot.end_min)
params.grounded_columns: time_slot.time_slot_id | time_slot.day | time_slot.start_hr | time_slot.start_min | time_slot.end_hr | time_slot.end_min
params.metric: start_time_text = printf('%02d:%02d', time_slot.start_hr, time_slot.start_min)  -- deterministic text formatting of the start time | end_time_text = printf('%02d:%02d', time_slot.end_hr, time_slot.end_min)      -- deterministic text formatting of the end time
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to section_with_course_instructor_room_time on time_slot_id — safe because section_with_course_instructor_room_time references a single time_slot_id per section row and this view is one-row-per-time_slot_id so joining will not duplicate the time-slot rows' columns (use a many-sections-to-one-time_slot relationship where sections are the many side). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension-like table keyed by time_slot_id (if present) on time_slot_id — safe when that other table is one-row-per-time_slot_id as well. | do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables (e.g., joins that would attach multiple sections, enrollments, or instructors per time_slot row) without re-aggregation on the many side first, because that would multiply time_slot rows' combinations and duplicate any measures derived from this view. If you need aggregated results per time_slot_id after joining to a many-side table, aggregate the many-side results (e.g., COUNT(section_id) GROUP BY time_slot_id) and then join the aggregated result back to time_slot_readable on time_slot_id. | When composing into larger queries, treat time_slot_readable as a dimension (lookup) that is one-row-per [time_slot_id, day, start_hr, start_min] (the declared grain). Joining from an aggregated fact (many rows per time_slot_id) into this view is safe; joining from this view into a many-row fact without aggregation on the fact will expand the result set as expected and may duplicate logical measures, so guard with appropriate GROUP BY or subquery aggregation.

views.description: Normalized time_slot with a human-readable start/end time strings. Use when presenting schedules or grouping by time ranges. Preserves original time components for analytical joins. | Use for: Display readable meeting times for schedules; Group sections by start time or time window; Filter time slots by human-readable range

views.name: course_popularity_by_enrollment
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tk.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(*) AS total_enrollments,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tk.ID) AS distinct_students
FROM takes tk
GROUP BY tk.course_id

params.description: Aggregate counts of enrollments and distinct students per course (one row per course_id).
params.when_to_use: Report total enrollments and number of unique students for a given course. | Compose course-level metrics into dashboards (e.g., enrollment trends, capacity planning) when joining to course/dimension tables. | Filter or aggregate courses by attributes (department, level) after joining to course dimension. | Compare per-course enrollments against other course-level aggregates (e.g., offerings per term).
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the course; derives from takes.course_id (tk.course_id) in the base takes table. | total_enrollments: integer count of enrollment rows for that course; derives from COUNT(*) over takes rows for the course. | distinct_students: integer count of distinct students enrolled in that course; derives from COUNT(DISTINCT takes.ID) where takes.ID is the student identifier in takes.
params.metric: total_enrollments = COUNT(*) over takes rows grouped by takes.course_id | distinct_students = COUNT(DISTINCT takes.ID) over takes rows grouped by takes.course_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course dimension (a table/view keyed by course_id) on course_id — safe because this view has exactly one row per course_id so its measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to aggregator views that are also one-row-per-course_id (if present) on course_id — safe because both sides are at the same grain. | do NOT directly join this view to any one-to-many child table or view keyed to course_id (for example: a sections table that has multiple sections per course, or section_with_course_instructor_room_time) without first aggregating that child to course_id. Doing so would duplicate total_enrollments and distinct_students because this view is at course_id grain and the child is many-per-course. | do NOT join to takes (the original base table) or any view that expands takes (e.g., takes_with_student_course_section) without re-aggregation; joining back to takes will multiply counts since takes has one row per enrollment. | If you need course-level measures combined with lower-grain details (e.g., per-section metrics), either: (a) re-aggregate the lower-grain data up to course_id before joining, or (b) join on course_id and then compute rates/ratios using window functions that partition by course_id while being careful to avoid summing these course-level aggregates across duplicated rows. | When composing with sibling aggregate views (course_offering_counts_by_term, student_enrollment_counts, instructor_salary_by_department, etc.), prefer joins on course_id only to views that are one-row-per-course_id; otherwise align grains by aggregating the many-side to course_id first. | Safe join examples: JOIN course dimension ON course_id; JOIN course_offering_counts_by_term (if that view is one-row-per-course_id) ON course_id. Unsafe join examples: JOIN section_with_course_instructor_room_time ON course_id (sections per course >1) without aggregating sections to course_id first; JOIN takes_with_student_course_section ON course_id is unsafe unless you aggregate that view to course_id.

views.description: Per-course aggregate enrollments across all terms: total enrollments and distinct student count. Useful for ranking course popularity, planning capacity, or identifying high-demand courses. | Use for: Which courses have the highest enrollment historically; Prepare inputs for capacity planning and course offering frequency; Identify courses with many unique students vs repeat enrollments
